coverage_claim: symbol-level: a symbol counts only if its Rust mapping compiles or its deviation is documented

packages.notes: archive::tar: Go-shaped Reader/Writer/Header over std::io with USTAR, PAX and GNU formats, long names, PAX time precision, sparse reading (old GNU, PAX 0.0/0.1/1.0) and format selection identical to Go (archives written by Go and Rust are byte-identical); Reader::next_raw returns byte-string headers like Go (Reader::next is the String form), times are SystemTime, ErrInsecurePath is opt-in (GODEBUG=tarinsecurepath=0 or Reader::set_reject_insecure_paths) and carries the header; sparse writing (Writer::write_sparse_header) is an extension because Go's is disabled; set_name_lookup is an extension that lets FileInfoHeader resolve names through rust_stdlib_sys::os::user

archive::zip: Go-shaped Reader/ReadCloser/Writer/File/FileHeader with ZIP64 read and write, data descriptors, extended timestamps, preambles, raw copy, registered compressors, UTF-8 flag and CP437 names (non-UTF-8 names decode as CP437 Strings and keep their exact bytes in raw_name/raw_comment; the writer stores those bytes as Go does), and the fs.FS view (Reader implements io::fs::FS); Modified is an instant without Go's zone, CreateHeader copies its header and exposes the updated copy, the DEFLATE compressor streams each member through flate::Writer at level 5 and is byte-identical to Go's, ErrInsecurePath is opt-in (GODEBUG=zipinsecurepath=0 or Reader::with_options); Reader<R> is generic over any ReadAt, including borrows such as &File and &[u8], and Reader::new / with_options return Result<Reader<R>, OpenError<R>> whose InsecurePath variant carries the usable reader (OpenError::into_reader; converting to io::Error drops it)

Go's buffer algorithms are reimplemented (std::io::BufReader cannot Peek, UnreadRune, ReadSlice or Discard with Go's rules): when a Read bypasses the buffer, ErrBufferFull, ReadLine's isPrefix and '\r' handling, UnreadByte/UnreadRune validity, ScanLines/ScanRunes/ScanWords, ErrTooLong growth and ErrFinalToken are Go's. Reader implements std::io::Read and BufRead (read_until keeps Go's read-ahead, so ReadBytes and ReadString are BufRead::read_until; Go strings are bytes, convert with String::from_utf8), Writer std::io::Write, so they drop into std code. Errors are the variants of rust_stdlib::bufio::Error (Error::is is errors.Is) inside io::Error; io.EOF is rust_stdlib::io::eof. Where Go returns data or a count with an error the error carries it: SliceError::data for ReadSlice, io::ReadError::read for Discard, io::CopyError::written for Write/WriteString; after a failed Peek Reader::buffer holds the available bytes. Scanner is an Iterator over tokens (Item = io::Result<Vec<u8>>): Scan/Bytes/Text is next, Err is the first Err item, Split and Buffer are builders, and a SplitFunc returns Result<Split> (Skip, Token, Last for ErrFinalToken); a negative advance cannot be expressed so a split function reports ErrNegativeAdvance itself, and Go's panics (empty tokens without progress, Split or Buffer after Scan) are error items. Counts are usize, so ErrNegativeCount is never returned by this API and ErrBadReadCount cannot occur because Rust's Read cannot report an impossible count. A Read returning Ok(0) into a non-empty buffer is EOF, so ErrNoProgress arises only from 100 consecutive Interrupted errors. Differences from Go that do not change results on conforming readers/writers: NewReader(Size)/NewWriter(Size) always allocate a new buffer instead of returning an already buffered argument; WriteTo/ReadFrom/WriteString do not use the underlying WriterTo/ReaderFrom/StringWriter fast paths; a write that accepts zero bytes of non-empty data is io.ErrShortWrite rather than a retry; Scanner::buffer takes a Vec and uses its capacity; SplitFunc tokens are copied into the scanner. Tested against Go by tools/io_check.py.

`&[u8]` carries Go's possibly-invalid UTF-8: `rust_stdlib::text::BytesExt` adds the Go functions std lacks for byte slices (invalid bytes are U+FFFD of width 1; case mapping, title casing and folding use rust_stdlib::unicode's Go tables, exact on every rune and compared by tools/bytes_check.py), and std slice methods are used where semantics match. Buffer and Reader keep Go's unread rules and capacity growth. Go index -1 is None; nil-versus-empty slices are not distinguished.
cmp: std Ord/PartialOrd for integers and strings; floats use rust_stdlib::math::compare for Go's NaN rules (NaN below everything and equal to itself, -0 == +0)

compress::bzip2: Streaming Reader with multi-stream, block/stream CRCs and Go's Huffman/StructuralError semantics; opt-in output and block-size Limits (unlimited output by default); truncation delivers Go's zero-filled partial output, checked against Go; decompression only, as in Go

compress::flate: Go-exact streaming inflate (byte-pull discipline, CorruptInputError offsets, preset dictionaries, Resetter) and a port of Go 1.27's compressor (the level 1-6 fast matchers, the level 7-9 lazy hash chains, Go's Huffman construction and block selection): output is byte-identical to Go's at levels -2..=9 for flate, zlib and gzip, including preset dictionaries and Flush schedules (checked by tools/flate_check.py; Go's own bytes are not covered by its compatibility promise, so a future Go may change them); I/O is std::io Read/BufRead/Write
compress::gzip: Reader (header fields, header CRC, multistream, Reset) and Writer (header, levels, Flush, Close, Reset) over flate; ModTime is Option<time::DateTime>, Extra is Option<Vec<u8>>

compress::lzw: Reader/Writer with Go's Close, Reset and latched errors over LSB/MSB widths 2..8; new_reader has no output budget (Reader::new takes an opt-in bound); constructors and Reset are infallible and report a bad litWidth on the first Read/Write/Close, as Go does, checked by tools/lzw_check.py; TIFF variant unsupported
compress::zlib: Reader/Writer over flate with preset dictionaries, FLEVEL header bits, Adler-32 checks and Resetter; Go's sentinel errors are Error constants carried in io::Error

container/heap: collections::heap::Heap keeps Go's sift algorithms, so the backing array order matches Go after any operation sequence; BinaryHeap is a max-heap with different sift order and has no remove or fix
container/list: index-arena list; Element is a Copy handle validated by list id and slot generation; List.Remove of an element of another list returns None
container/ring: Rc/RefCell nodes (next strong, prev weak); nil ring is Option::None

context: Go's cancellation tree on std threads/condvars (event driven, one lazy timer thread). Context is a concrete handle; constructors are methods (Context::background, ctx.with_cancel()) (custom Context implementations are not supported); deadlines are Instants; Done is a handle with wait/wait_timeout/receiver; keys are typed Key<T>. AfterFunc firing order among siblings is unspecified (as in Go). Rust adds Context::check as a convenience.

rust-stdlib-crypto: the Hash identifiers with New, Available, Size, HashFunc, String and RegisterHash. MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 are registered; MD4, RIPEMD-160, BLAKE2, MD5SHA1 and MLDSAMu exist as variants but are unavailable, as in a Go program that does not import their packages. The key, signing, decryption and KEM interfaces are traits: PublicKey, PrivateKey and DecrypterOpts are aliases of dyn Any (Go's empty interface); Go's nil rand reader is None; Go's signer.(MessageSigner) type assertion, which a trait object cannot express, is the provided method Signer::as_message_signer that SignMessage consults. The key types implement them: ed25519, ecdsa, rsa and mldsa private keys are Signers (rsa also a Decrypter, with Hash and the packages' option types as SignerOpts through SignerOpts::as_any), and the mlkem keys are Encapsulators and Decapsulators.

rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto aes. NewCipher returns an aes::Cipher that implements cipher::Block; the key-size error is aes::KeySizeError with Go's message. Go's panics on short buffers are Errs with Go's messages.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the RustCrypto cbc, cfb-mode, ctr, ofb and aes-gcm crates. Block, Stream, BlockMode and AEAD are traits (Block, Stream, BlockMode, Aead); constructors return boxed trait objects borrowing the Block. Go panics (wrong IV or nonce length, short output, input not full blocks, wrong nonce length given to GCM) are Err(cipher::Error) carrying Go's panic message; errOpen is Error::is_authentication_failure. Rust's borrow rules make Go's 'invalid buffer overlap' panics unreachable; the exact-overlap idiom is covered by the *_in_place methods, and Seal/Open append to a Vec like Go's dst. Modes accept any Block with an 8 or 16 byte block size (every Go block cipher); GCM requires 16. NewGCMWithNonceSize supports the nonce sizes in cipher::GCM_NONCE_SIZES (1-32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 56, 60, 64, 72, 80, 96, 100, 112, 120, 128, 192, 256) because the aes-gcm crate fixes the size at compile time; Go accepts any positive size. io.Closer has no Rust equivalent, so StreamWriter::close flushes the underlying writer and drops it.
rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto des. NewCipher and NewTripleDESCipher return des::Cipher and des::TripleDesCipher, which implement cipher::Block; neither rejects weak keys, as in Go.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed RustCrypto dsa crate (0.7.0, with its hazmat feature for the private key type and pkcs8 for PKIX DER). Embedding is a public field plus Deref; *big.Int fields are bigint::Int. The crate supports the FIPS 186-3 parameter sizes only and truncates a hash longer than Q to its leftmost N/8 bytes (Go reduces it modulo Q and leaves truncation to the caller); Go's panics become false/errors.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed p256, p384, p521 and x25519-dalek crates. Curve is a sealed trait whose values are the four functions (curves compare by name); keys are structs with Go's validation order and error messages, and add PKIX/PKCS#8 DER hooks for x509. Like Go 1.26+ without GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1, GenerateKey ignores the reader and uses crypto/rand (including cryptotest.SetGlobalRandom).

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed p224, p256, p384, p521 and ecdsa crates. Embedding (PrivateKey embeds PublicKey, PublicKey embeds elliptic.Curve) is a public field plus Deref; the *big.Int fields are bigint::Int. Randomized signing is the hedged RFC 6979 variant with entropy from crypto/rand, the reader arguments are ignored like Go 1.26+ without GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1, and signing with no reader is deterministic RFC 6979 over the hash named by the options, as in Go. Keys on a custom elliptic.CurveParams can be held but signing and verifying return an error (Go's math/big fallback is a first-party ECDSA implementation, ADR 0003). PrivateKey implements crypto::Signer; PKIX, PKCS #8 and SEC 1 DER hooks serve x509.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed ed25519-dalek and sha2 crates. PublicKey and PrivateKey are newtypes over Go's byte slices (a private key is the seed followed by the public key); Go's panics on bad key lengths are errors with Go's messages, and Verify returns Result<bool>. Signing rejects a private key whose public half does not match its seed, where Go signs with whatever half the key carries (deviation mismatched-public-half-rejected). The key types implement crypto::Signer (PrivateKey) and add PKIX/PKCS#8 DER hooks for x509. ed25519-dalek has no Ed25519ctx (a context without prehashing), so Options with a context and no hash return an error. The crate pulls the proc-macro crate curve25519-dalek-derive on x86-64 (ADR 0003).

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed p224, p256, p384 and p521 crates. Curve is a trait, curves are Arc<dyn Curve> (P256() returns the same object every time, and elliptic::same_curve compares them like Go's interface ==); the *big.Int coordinates are the non-negative bigint::Int. Like Go the point operations panic on points that are not on the curve. Copies of the NIST curve parameters keep working (they delegate to the same crates as long as no field was modified). Go's generic CurveParams arithmetic for arbitrary curves is a first-party elliptic-curve implementation, so on a CurveParams that is not one of the four NIST curves the arithmetic methods panic with an explanatory message (ADR 0003).

rust-stdlib-crypto: the reviewed RustCrypto crates are not a validated FIPS 140-3 module, so the mode cannot be enabled. Enabled and Enforced are always false, Version is Go's "latest", and WithoutEnforcement only runs its function.

rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto hkdf (SimpleHkdf). Hash constructors as for crypto/hmac. Info is any AsRef<[u8]>, a superset of Go's string. Like Go, Expand accepts pseudorandom keys shorter than the hash size (zero-padded, which HMAC makes equivalent) and errors above 255*HashLen.

rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto hmac (SimpleHmac, so SHA-3 works too). New takes a constructor of any hash of this crate (sha256::new, a closure returning crypto::Hash::new, ...) and returns an error for other hash.Hash implementations, which RustCrypto cannot key without knowing the algorithm. Equal runs on the subtle crate.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed hpke crate (rozbb/rust-hpke 0.14.1, MIT OR Apache-2.0) with p256/p384/p521/x25519-dalek, HKDF and the AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs. KEM, KDF, AEAD, PublicKey and PrivateKey are sealed traits over runtime-selected suites; Seal output is enc followed by the ciphertext, as in Go. The RFC 9180 test vectors of Go (rfc9180.json, 1000 encryptions and exports per suite) pass. The post-quantum KEMs and SHAKE KDFs are documented deviations.
rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto md-5. State methods (marshal_binary and friends) are inherent on Digest and emit Go's md5\x01 format; Clone is std Clone and hash::Hash::clone_hash.
rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed RustCrypto ml-dsa crate (0.1.1). Private keys are the 32-byte seeds; PrivateKey implements crypto::Signer. crypto.MLDSAMu is Hash::MlDsaMu.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed RustCrypto ml-kem crate (0.3.2). Decapsulation keys are the 64-byte seeds; the keys implement crypto::Decapsulator and crypto::Encapsulator. Decapsulate rejects only a wrong ciphertext length (implicit rejection otherwise), like Go.
rust-stdlib-crypto: derandomized ML-KEM encapsulation for known-answer tests, over the ml-kem crate.

rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto pbkdf2 with HMAC. Password is any AsRef<[u8]> (a superset of Go's string); the iteration count is a u32 where Go takes an int, and zero acts as one like Go. Errors for zero or too-large key lengths carry Go's messages.

rust-stdlib-crypto over getrandom (operating-system generator). Read panics where Go crashes on failure; Reader implements std::io::Read and reports system errors. Int and Prime use bigint::Int (this crate's non-negative integer) and crypto-primes' Baillie-PSW test; Int consumes the reader exactly as Go does, Prime follows Go's candidate shaping and honours the reader only with GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1 like Go 1.26+.

rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto rc4. Cipher also implements cipher::Stream. XORKeyStream returns an Err where Go indexes out of range (dst shorter than src); Reset leaves a cipher whose key stream is all zeros, as in Go.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed rsa (0.10.0-rc.19), crypto-bigint and crypto-primes crates; the rsa crate carries RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin timing attack on private-key operations, no patched release), recorded in docs/crypto-dependencies.json, ADR 0003 and the module documentation. *big.Int fields are bigint::Int and E is i64. hash.Hash arguments (OAEP) are crypto::Hash identifiers because the crate selects digests by type. OAEP encryption and PSS signing honour the supplied reader as Go does; GenerateKey and EncryptPKCS1v15 ignore it like Go 1.26+ unless GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1, and GODEBUG=rsa1024min=0 allows keys below 1024 bits. PrivateKey implements crypto::Signer and crypto::Decrypter; PKCS #1, PKCS #8 and PKIX DER hooks serve x509.
rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto sha1. State methods are inherent on Digest and emit Go's sha\x01 format.
rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto sha2. State methods are inherent on Digest and emit Go's sha\x02 (224) and sha\x03 (256) formats.

rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto sha3 (SHA3-224..512) and cshake (SHAKE and cSHAKE; empty name and customization give SHAKE, as in Go). Sha3 marshals Go's sha\x08 format by translating the sha3 crate's public SerializableState bytes; only the absorbing direction exists for it, so Go states whose direction byte is 1 (not producible from Go's public SHA3 API) are rejected. Shake.write fails with an io::Error where Go panics 'Write after Read'. Shake additionally implements std::io::Read and Clone.
rust-stdlib-crypto over RustCrypto sha2. State methods are inherent on Digest and emit Go's sha\x04 to sha\x07 formats.

rust-stdlib-crypto over the subtle crate. ConstantTimeCopy and XORBytes panic with Go's messages. WithDataIndependentTiming is a deviation: stable Rust has no safe way to set the CPU's data-independent timing mode, so the function only runs its argument.

rust-stdlib-tls::tls over Rustls with the ring provider (docs/adr/0002): no first-party TLS state machine or cryptography. Go's `net.Conn` is `rust_stdlib::net::Conn` (tls::Conn implements it); `*x509.Certificate` and `*x509.CertPool` are the DER-reading stand-ins in tls::x509 because backends/tls cannot depend on crates/crypto (the two locks resolve getrandom and zeroize at different versions and the dependency policy forbids duplicate package names); crypto.PrivateKey is the PrivateKey enum (PKCS #1/#8/SEC 1 DER or a Rustls SigningKey). Go callbacks are `Arc<dyn Fn>` fields; Go `error` is tls::Error whose variants are Go's concrete error types. Certificate verification is webpki's with Go's x509 error texts (checked by tools/gotls_check.py). Where Rustls deliberately refuses a Go option (TLS 1.0/1.1, renegotiation, RC4/3DES/CBC suites, static RSA, P-521 and post-quantum groups, SHA-1 signatures, Encrypted Client Hello, external ticket keys) the entry is a `rustls-policy` deviation and the option fails with an explicit error rather than being ignored. InsecureSkipVerify exists only because Go exposes it. Not honoured or different, each recorded per symbol: nil RootCAs/ClientCAs on macOS (no-platform-verifier), TLSUnique/SCTs, WrapSession/UnwrapSession, QUIC secrets (keys are provided instead).

rust-stdlib-crypto::x509 over the reviewed key types (docs/adr/0003). Go's encoding/asn1, net, net/url, time, math/big and encoding/pem types are stand-ins defined in the module: ObjectIdentifier (asn1.ObjectIdentifier), Ip/IpNet (net.IP, *net.IPNet), url::Url (*url.URL), Time (time.Time; instants carry no location, so error text prints UTC), BigInt (*big.Int) and pem::Block. Go's crypto.PublicKey/PrivateKey `any` values are the PublicKey and PrivateKey enums. Go's error interface is the Error enum, whose variants are Go's concrete error types. Parsing and verification are Go's portable code paths; error text of encoding/asn1 based paths (ParsePKCS1/8/EC keys, ParsePKIXPublicKey, ParseCertificateRequest, ParseDERCRL) is not reproduced for malformed input, though acceptance is.

rust-stdlib-crypto::x509::pkix. AttributeTypeAndValue.Value (Go any) is the Value enum; asn1.ObjectIdentifier, asn1.BitString, asn1.RawValue and time.Time are the stand-ins defined in the x509 module. Name.ExtraNames is an Option<Vec<_>> because Go's Name.String distinguishes a nil ExtraNames from an empty one. The `type` fields are named type_.

database/sql: Go's pool, Tx, Stmt, Rows and Scan conversions ported from sql.go and convert.go on std::sync; any becomes driver::Arg (arguments) and &mut dyn Scanner (destinations); optional driver interfaces are as_* accessors; RawBytes copies; Go strings with invalid UTF-8 scan into String lossily; uuid.UUID is a Scanner destination, cursor-valued columns are not supported (closed-interface); Rows/Conn/Stmt release on drop and a dropped Tx rolls back; tests run against the fakedb port in examples/common/fakedb.rs

database/sql/driver: every interface is a trait; optional interfaces are as_* accessors on Conn, Stmt and Rows; Value is an enum, Arg is Go's any; ValueConverters, IsValue, RowsAffected, ResultNoRows ported from types.go and driver.go; Go's unexported decimalDecompose and decimalCompose are the Decompose and Compose traits over the Decimal parts, which drivers receive as Value::Decimal, and a uuid.UUID argument converts to its string

embed::FS is a read-only fs over (name, bytes) pairs built from include_bytes!. Go's //go:embed directive has no Rust equivalent: rust_stdlib::embed_files! lists files by path (declarative), and the first-party proc macro rust_stdlib_derive::embed! (crates/derive) walks directories and wildcard patterns with Go's rules ('.'/'_' names skipped in directories unless 'all:', no matches is a compile error). FS::open/read_dir/read_file are also the io::fs FS, ReadDirFS and ReadFileFS impls; files are 0444, directories ModeDir|0555, mod times zero, and error values match Go's.
encoding: Go's marshal/unmarshal/append interfaces as traits; errors are Box<dyn Error> and AppendX writes into a caller Vec<u8>
encoding::ascii85: Buffered and incremental encoding/decoding with Go-compatible shorthand and whitespace

encoding::asn1: DER parse/marshal with Go's strictness rules via typed Marshal/Unmarshal traits, Decoder/Encoder SEQUENCE mapping and Params (Go tag syntax); Go's reflection-based Marshal/Unmarshal are deviations; explicit tag wrapper length is ignored as in Go unless Options::strict_explicit; default depth 256 (Go 10000, stack safety); year 0000 and +/-24h offsets rejected; negative OID arcs rejected on marshal

encoding::base32: one Engine type with Go's behaviour (CR/LF skipped, Go's CorruptInputError offsets and partial output on error via decode_into), differential-checked by tools/base32_check.py. Decoding is a port of Go's quantum state machine. Engine::new and with_padding return Result where Go panics; Engine::new takes a 32-byte array, so a wrong alphabet length cannot be expressed. with_padding takes Option<u8>, so padding above 0xff, which Go rejects, cannot be expressed. encode returns a String (U+FFFD for a non-UTF-8 byte of a custom alphabet); encode_to_vec returns the raw bytes. Decoder is a port of Go's stream decoder (1024-byte buffer, per-read newline filtering), so data after padding is an error only when it arrives in a later chunk and corrupt offsets are chunk-relative, as Go; where Go returns data with an error, Decoder returns the data and then the error on the next read. The differential also compares chunked-read schedules (caller buffer size and source bytes per read) record by record

encoding::base64: one Engine type with Go's behaviour (non-strict, CR/LF skipped, partial output on error via decode_into), differential-checked by tools/base64_parity_check.py. Engine::new and with_padding return Result where Go panics.

encoding::binary: Go's ByteOrder and AppendByteOrder traits with BigEndian, LittleEndian and NativeEndian; fixed-size values through the FixedSize trait; Go-compatible varints, differential-checked by tools/encoding_conformance.py. Deviations forced by Rust: Go's reflection-based Read, Write, Size, Encode, Decode and Append accept only FixedSize types (bool, 8 to 64-bit integers, floats, slices and arrays of them), and structs are rejected at compile time instead of at run time; ByteOrder covers the 16, 32 and 64-bit operations that Go defines. Fallible calls return io::Result where Go panics on short buffers (put and buffer-form calls report UnexpectedEof; overflow reports InvalidData). Read and ReadUvarint report io.EOF and io.ErrUnexpectedEOF as io::Error values of kind UnexpectedEof carrying crate::io::Error::Eof or crate::io::Error::UnexpectedEof. Append and AppendUvarint return () and extend the Vec in place

encoding::csv: Go's Reader and Writer ported from Go's line-based readRecord and Write, with Go's quoting, CRLF, comment, TrimLeadingSpace, LazyQuotes, FieldsPerRecord and ParseError messages; differential-checked by tools/encoding_conformance.py (Read event sequences with positions and offsets, and WriteAll output). Deviations forced by Rust: Comma and Comment are chars, and Comment None is Go's zero rune; Read returns Result<Option<Vec<String>>, Error>, with None at end of input; Reader::read_raw is Go's Read: byte fields, with the partial record returned alongside parse, field-count and I/O errors (checked with injected read failures and invalid UTF-8); Reader::read is the Result-shaped String form; TrailingComma has no effect, as in Go; FieldPos panics out of range as Go does; Writer.Flush and WriteAll return io::Result and Writer.Error returns the sticky error as an Option. Limits are Rust-only opt-in input budgets, unlimited by default

encoding::gob follows Go's gob byte for byte: type ids (predefined 1..23, user ids from 64 in first-sent order), wire types, field-number deltas, zero omission, pointer flattening, interface values by registered name with inline type definitions, GobEncoder/BinaryMarshaler types, and the decoder's compile step (compatibility checks, ignored fields, overflow and corrupt-data error texts, including Go's behaviour of reading type ids). Values come from rust_stdlib::reflect, so any #[derive(Reflect)] type works. Verified by tools/gob_check.py, a differential against Go over generated typed values (equal bytes, cross-decoding, merges, schema evolution, corrupted streams). Rust-shaped differences: Encode and Decode take any Reflect type (Decode copies in and out through reflect::edit); Decode(nil) is decode_discard; errors are std::io::Error with the io sentinels for EOF; a GobEncoder or BinaryMarshaler is a type with #[reflect_methods] methods of those Go names; a Rust map built from a Rust value is never nil, so an empty map field is sent where Go omits a nil map (values built with reflect::zero/new keep Go's nil maps).
encoding::hex: Go's Encode/Decode/Append*/Dump/Dumper and error values, differential-checked by tools/hex_check.py

encoding::json follows Go 1.27's behaviour (v1 implemented on v2) byte for byte: Marshal/Unmarshal/Decoder/Encoder map to the Serialize/Deserialize traits (derive macros take Go struct tags), the scanner, Compact/Indent/HTMLEscape, token stream and error values (text, offsets, paths) are differential-tested against Go, and Value is the interface{} target. Rust-shaped differences: Unmarshal returns the decoded value rather than filling a pointer (unmarshal_into and Decoder::decode_into decode into an existing value with Go's merge rules), and nil versus empty slices/maps do not exist (Vec/BTreeMap are always empty, Option is nil); Value objects are insertion-ordered (struct fields in declaration order, map keys and decoded text sorted); reflect.Type fields are Go-style type name strings; Bytes is the []byte-as-base64 type; Value parses with FromStr and prints with Display.

jsontext is a port of Go 1.27's package: the Decoder and Encoder state machines, read-buffer management, offsets, JSON Pointers, RFC 8785 canonicalization and error text are checked against Go by tools/jsontext_check.py. Rust shapes: Options is a set rather than an interface, a Token owns its text, an empty Value stands for nil and empty, accessors returning (T, error) return (T, Option<Error>), and every error value is a variant of jsontext::Error (Error::is compares sentinels).

v2 is a typed port of Go 1.27's package on top of jsontext. Go finds conversions with reflect; here a type implements MarshalTo or UnmarshalFrom (the standard types do, and rust_stdlib_derive::{MarshalTo, UnmarshalFrom} derive them for structs from the #[json(...)] attributes: Go struct tags plus omitempty, omitzero, string, case_ignore, case_strict, inline, unknown (Go's embed option on a map or Value) and format). Error text, byte offsets, JSON Pointers, partial results after errors, merging into existing values and every option are checked against Go by tools/jsonv2_check.py. Rust shapes: an empty Vec or map is both Go's nil and empty (omitzero, FormatNil*AsNull), Go's any is v2::Any, []byte is json::Bytes, pointers are Option, the format tag option is rejected as in Go unless experimental_support_format_tag is set, and time.Time/time.Duration formats and the v1 compatibility options are not supported.

encoding::pem: Textual blocks, sorted headers, first-valid-block/remainder decoding and opt-in budgets; Block metadata is UTF-8, RawBlock/decode_raw carries Go's arbitrary bytes, differential-checked by tools/pem_check.py

encoding::xml: Go's tokenizer (byte-exact errors, line numbers and offsets, name spaces, Strict/AutoClose/Entity/CharsetReader), Encoder and struct-tag Marshal/Unmarshal through the Marshal/Unmarshal traits and the rust-stdlib-derive macros. Documented differences: float digits are chosen by Rust's shortest formatter with ties resolved like Go; type strings in error messages are Rust type names; invalid UTF-8 bytes inside names show as U+FFFD; Decoder recursion is bounded by a stack budget (max_unmarshal_stack, default 1 MiB) as well as Go's depth limit, because it recurses on the native thread stack

errors: std::error::Error is the error interface; Unwrap is Error::source and As is downcast_ref. rust_stdlib::error adds what std lacks: Joined (Join), Message (New, ErrUnsupported; compared by identity), and is/find, which walk source chains and Joined trees depth first.

rust_stdlib::expvar: Var (a trait whose Display output is valid JSON), Int and Float (atomic; Float.Add is a compare-exchange loop on the bits), String, Map (sorted keys; Map::add and add_float recognize Int and Float through Var::as_int and Var::as_float, the Rust form of Go's type assertion), Func, publish/get/iter and the published constructors over a process-wide registry. JSON rendering follows expvar's own quoting (appendJSONQuote), the expanded layout of the handler, and encoding/json (json::marshal) for Func. tests/expvar.rs ports expvar_test.go (the handler and quoting tables included); tools/expvar_check.py runs 400 seeded scripts (7,395 operation records) against Go, comparing every rendered value and duplicate-name panic exactly.

flag: Go's grammar, error texts and PrintDefaults layout on FlagSet and the command-line set. Flag variables are shared Ptr<T> handles instead of *T. Rust substitutions for reflection: Value has provided is_bool_flag/kind/zero_string/as_getter methods (a custom value without zero_string counts as zero when its default text is empty; a panicking String on a zero value is not caught), usage callbacks take &FlagSet (the package-level readers work from inside the command-line usage on a snapshot; modifying the set there panics), Set records the caller through #[track_caller].

fmt: Rust's format!/print!/write!/Display/Debug achieve Printf and Stringer for formats known at compile time (mapped to std). The `printf` module keeps Go's verb engine only for runtime Go-format strings and the differential suite, over an explicit operand model. Go's reflection over `any` operands becomes the Value enum (Arg alias) with From impls for Rust primitives, strings, Vec/array/slice, Option/Box (pointers) and HashMap/BTreeMap; named Go types with methods are Value::Named carrying Display (Go's Stringer), Debug (Go's GoStringer), Formatter and error implementations. Printing is byte exact: every verb, flag, width, precision, `*` and [n] argument index, and the %!verb(type=value), EXTRA, MISSING, BADINDEX, BADWIDTH, BADPREC, NOVERB and PANIC error forms; digits and quoting come from strconv. Panicking String/Error/Format methods are caught with catch_unwind (the default panic hook still reports to stderr). Sprint* return String (invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD; append* are byte exact; Fprint*/Print* are std::write!/print!); Errorf returns fmt::WrapError (std::error::Error; source() is the first %w operand, sources() is Go's Unwrap() []error). Scan* write into ScanArg destinations (typed &mut, `*[]byte` as Vec<u8>, custom Scanner); Fscan* take std::io::Read (one rune of lookahead is lost, as in Go) or, as fscan_runes/fscanln_runes/fscanf_runes, an io::RuneScanner. Not expressible: scanning into pointers to renamed (named) Go types via reflect (use the underlying type's destination), reflect.Value operands, and Printf of arbitrary Go values (build them as Value); %p and %v of pointers print the address carried by the Value. A Rust i32 operand is a Go int32 (use isize or Value::int for Go int) and char is a Go rune (int32).
Traits over std::io::Write/Read implemented by the crate's adler32, crc32, crc64 and fnv digests and by maphash.Hash. XOF is the trait only; SHAKE lives in the cryptography crate.
hash::adler32 (compress::adler32 retained): Incremental Adler32 digest and Go binary state
hash::crc32 (compress::crc32 retained): IEEE/Castagnoli/Koopman/custom polynomials, incremental digests and Go binary state
hash::crc64: ISO/ECMA/custom polynomial incremental checksums; Go-compatible binary state serialization
hash::fnv: FNV-1/FNV-1a 32/64/128-bit incremental digests; Go-compatible binary state serialization

SipHash-1-3 (std DefaultHasher) keyed by prefixing the seed. Values are implementation-defined (as in Go) and differ between processes; the differential compares properties (streaming equals one-shot, chunking independence, Sum layout, seed sensitivity). Comparable values hash through std::hash::Hash.
html: Text escaping and Go-compatible named/numeric character-reference decoding

html/template: contextual autoescaping is a port of Go's escaper (context, transition, escape, js, css, url, html). Typed content types are newtypes converting to named template values; errors are TemplateError::Escape(Error) with Go's ErrorCode values and messages. Escaper edits go to a copy of the parse tree, so call Template::tree after the first execution. An unvalidated MarshalJSON result is compacted but only syntax-checked with Go's scanner messages; strings are UTF-8.

image: Point/Rectangle geometry and the Image/PalettedImage/RGBA64Image traits; RGBA/RGBA64/NRGBA/NRGBA64/Gray/Gray16/Alpha/Alpha16/CMYK/Paletted/Uniform and YCbCr/NYCbCrA with Go's accessors and Set semantics; Pix/Y/Cb/Cr/A are Pix windows onto shared buffers so SubImage shares pixels like Go slices (Clone copies); Uniform is its own color model; format registry over the crate's PNG and GIF codecs; Decode returns a Box<dyn Image> and the format name, errors are DecodeError (io::Error plus the format name)

image::color: every Go color type (RGBA/RGBA64/NRGBA/NRGBA64/Gray/Gray16/Alpha/Alpha16/YCbCr/NYCbCrA/CMYK) and model with Go-exact conversion arithmetic, Palette, and ModelFunc; Color is a closed enum of those types, so user-defined colors are not expressible; Palette.Convert returns None where Go returns nil; ModelFunc accepts capturing closures and compares by identity
image::color::palette: Plan9 and WebSafe tables generated from Go's package; checked entry-by-entry against Go by tools/palette_check.py

image::draw: Draw/DrawMask with Go's clipping, fast paths and generic RGBA64 arithmetic (Over/Src, any mask), FloydSteinberg, Drawer/Quantizer/RGBA64Image traits; self-draw via draw_within; Quantizer takes an explicit capacity; a paletted index outside the palette and FloydSteinberg on an empty palette panic as in Go

image::gif: Decode/DecodeAll/DecodeConfig with Go's validation and leniencies plus explicit Limits; byte-identical Encode (Options: NumColors/Quantizer/Drawer) and EncodeAll; zero Config is None; failed encodes write nothing; Decode returns the first frame as Paletted rather than image.Image

image::jpeg: a port of Go's decoder and encoder. Decode reads baseline, extended and progressive JPEGs (restart markers, all standard and Go 1.27 flex sampling ratios, grayscale, YCbCr, RGB, Adobe CMYK/YCCK) with Go's IDCT, leniencies and error texts, and returns Box<dyn Image> holding Gray, Ycbcr, Rgba or Cmyk; Encode is byte-identical to Go for every input image type; FormatError/UnsupportedError are payloads of io::Error; registered with image::decode as "jpeg". Go panics on a few malformed inputs (a Huffman table that indexes outside its values, a block outside its plane); the Rust decoder returns a FormatError instead

image::png: All color types/depths, Adam7, PLTE/tRNS, CRC checks and explicit Limits; Go color-type selection on encode; compression through zlib::Writer at Go's levels, so the whole file is byte-identical to Go's for every image type and level; no interlaced or custom-filter encoding; IDAT chunks after the one the zlib stream ends in are skipped as Go skips them, bytes after the stream inside that chunk are rejected (deviation idat-tail-bytes on Decode); EncoderBuffer reuses the output allocation; a bad palette fails after the signature and IHDR are written, as in Go; FormatError/UnsupportedError are payloads of io::Error

rust_stdlib::index::suffixarray: suffix array built by prefix doubling (the array of a text is unique, so lookups and the serialized form match Go's SA-IS); Write reproduces Go's byte layout, including the stale bytes in its 10-byte size slots (tools/suffixarray_check.py compares 33k write, read, lookup and FindAllIndex vectors with Go). Index owns a copy of the data where Go keeps the caller's slice. tests/suffixarray.rs ports the test cases, the lookup and FindAllIndex checks, the corrupt-stream tests and a construction check through the serialized suffix array.

Reader/Writer/Seeker are std::io::Read/Write/Seek and the composite interfaces are trait bounds. Go's io.EOF is Ok(0) from Read (std convention) and an io::Error carrying rust_stdlib::io::Error::Eof elsewhere (rust_stdlib::io::eof, is_eof); the other error variables are the variants of rust_stdlib::io::Error (Error::is is errors.Is). Go's (n, err) results are Result values whose error carries the count: CopyError::written for Copy/CopyBuffer/CopyN and ReadError::read for ReadFull/ReadAtLeast/ReadAt. Copy/CopyBuffer/CopyN (kept for Go's partial count and ErrShortWrite) do not dispatch to WriterTo/ReaderFrom nor shrink the buffer for a LimitedReader; CopyBuffer with an empty buffer is an error where Go panics; a negative Go count for CopyN is zero. ReaderAt/WriterAt keep Go's contract (the buffer is filled unless an error, io.EOF included, says why not) with u64 offsets like std's FileExt; an offset above i64::MAX is Go's negative offset. MultiWriter does not flatten or forward optional interfaces; a Read that returns Ok(0) for a non-empty buffer is EOF (so ErrNoProgress is produced only by repeated Interrupted); dropping a pipe half does not close it, as in Go. Pipe halves are cloneable handles; PipeWriter::write_shared reports the bytes consumed before an error and PipeReader::read_raw is Read with Go's exact result, including Ok(0) for a zero-length write. Tested against Go by tools/io_check.py.

Interfaces are traits (rust_stdlib::io::fs); File extends std::io::Read. Go finds optional interfaces with type assertions, which Rust trait objects cannot do, so FS has as_glob_fs/as_read_dir_fs/as_read_file_fs/as_stat_fs/as_sub_fs/as_read_link_fs hooks that an implementation overrides; Glob, ReadDir, ReadFile, Stat, Sub, Lstat and ReadLink consult them exactly where Go asserts. Errors are io::Error: a PathError is the payload (fs::path_error recovers it, its kind is the inner error's) and the sentinel variables are variants of fs::Error (Error::is is errors.Is; ERR_NOT_EXIST etc. also match by io::ErrorKind so std::fs errors qualify). Names are &str, so ValidPath's UTF-8 check is implied; WalkDirFunc is a closure trait over (path, Option<&dyn DirEntry>, Option<io::Error>) -> io::Result<()>; ReadDir returns ReadDirError, which carries the entries read before a failure (Go returns both). First-party implementations: DirFS (os.DirFS over std::fs, with ReadLinkFS), MapFS (testing/fstest.MapFS, resolving symlinks in Open, Lstat and ReadLink) and embed::FS. Tested against Go with fstest.MapFS by tools/io_check.py.
Deprecated package: every function is std (std::fs, std::io) or its os replacement (os::create_temp, os::mkdir_temp).
iter: any Iterator is a Seq (and an iterator of pairs is a Seq2); Pull is Iterator::fuse, and dropping the iterator is stop

log: Go's text logger with Go's exact line format over std::io::Write. Local time is Go's time.Local: TZ and ZONEINFO are read as in Go (rust_stdlib::time::local), and LUTC prints UTC; checked by tools/log_check.py under America/New_York. Deviations forced by Rust std: ...any operands are std::fmt::Arguments; Output's calldepth is ignored (the #[track_caller] chain picks the reported call site); Fatal exits the process and Panic panics with the message String payload as in Go. The earlier JSON-line logger moved to log::json.

log/slog: a port of Go's commonHandler state machine over std, byte-identical to Go's TextHandler and JSONHandler (checked by tools/log_check.py). Deviations forced by Rust std: ...any lists are &[Arg]; any payloads implement Dynamic (text/JSON renderings, error and downcast hooks) because Rust has no reflection; strings are valid UTF-8 so Go's invalid-UTF-8 repairs never occur; Record.PC is a #[track_caller] Location and Source.Function is empty; times are time::DateTime, and the default time is Go's Local zone (TZ as in Go, via rust_stdlib::time::local); LogValuer panics carry no stack trace.

log/syslog: Go's syslog client over std::net (UDP, TCP) and std::os::unix::net (unixgram, unix) with Go's message format. Deviations forced by Rust std: the host name is read from /proc/sys/kernel/hostname, /etc/hostname, the hostname command or HOSTNAME (no gethostname); timestamps follow Go: the RFC 3339 stamp carries the local offset and the local stamp uses Local time (TZ as in Go).
maps: std HashMap and BTreeMap methods; iteration order of HashMap is unspecified (Go: random), BTreeMap iterates in key order.

Rust std (f64/f32 methods, integer constants) where it matches Go; first-party ports of Go's algorithms (from FreeBSD msun, bit-identical to Go's portable code) for everything whose std result differs from Go's: trigonometry, inverse trigonometry, hyperbolics, exp/log families, pow, hypot, cbrt, erf, gamma and Bessel; NaN() is Go's bit pattern 0x7FF8000000000001. int is i64 and uint is usize (the surface is 64-bit). The differential compares bit patterns against an amd64 Go oracle where one can run (Go on arm64 fuses x*y+z, which changes the last bits of Go's own code; a native arm64 oracle is accepted with wider tolerances). Subnormal arguments of log-based functions and exp near overflow are skipped, because Go's amd64 assembly is inaccurate there. Every result is bit-identical except the symbols marked platform-float, which inherit the last-bit differences of Go's platform-specific assembly Exp. NaN payloads are not compared.

math/bits: std integer methods. Len is BITS - leading_zeros; RotateLeft is rotate_left with the count masked to the width (a negative count rotates right); Add and Sub chain two overflowing_add/overflowing_sub; Mul, Div and Rem widen to u128 (Div panics when y <= hi, Rem when y == 0). Counts are u32 where Go returns int; uint is usize.

Go's complex128 is rust_stdlib::strconv::Complex (with Add/Sub/Mul/Neg and Go's Div, which is the runtime's complex128div). Algorithms, special values and branch cuts are Go's; only the real functions they call are this crate's math ports.
math::rand::v1: NewSource lagged Fibonacci and all Rand methods incl. Read and Zipf bit-identical to Go amd64/arm64; Seed is the Go 1.24+ default no-op; Source64 is folded into Source
math::rand: Seeded PCG/ChaCha8 (marshal, Read) and all Rand methods, Zipf bit-identical to Go amd64/arm64; OS-seeded per-thread non-CSPRNG globals

mime: Go's ParseMediaType/FormatMediaType grammar with RFC 2231 values, Go's extension registry (built-in table, unix mime database, AddExtensionType) and RFC 2047 word encoding/decoding with a charset hook; differential-checked by tools/mime_check.py. AddExtensionType quotes the extension in its error as Go does. Deviations: decoded RFC 2231 values and words that are not UTF-8 are errors, not raw bytes; ExtensionsByType returns an empty Vec for nil; FormatMediaType and TypeByExtension return None for ""; Windows registry is not read

multipart: Go's Writer, Reader (NextPart, NextRawPart, ReadForm) with Go's lenient framing, Form/FileHeader/File and Part names, differential-checked by tools/multipart_check.py. Part is an io::Read over the underlying stream that borrows the Reader (Go's rule that the next part discards the rest of the current one holds; Part::into_owned buffers it), text is Strings (non-UTF-8 headers and form values are errors), and ReadForm keeps file parts in memory up to maxMemory and spills larger ones to multipart-* temporary files in TMPDIR exactly as Go does (one shared file unless GODEBUG=multipartfiles=distinct; Form.RemoveAll deletes them and, as in Go, dropping a Form does not).
quotedprintable: Buffered via std I/O, text/binary encoding and bounded incremental decoding

net maps Go's package onto std::net and std::os::unix::net. Errors are one enum, NetError, over Go's concrete error types (OpError, AddrError, DNSError, ...); Read/Write return Ok(0) at end of stream instead of io.EOF; interface values become the Addr/Conn/Listener/PacketConn traits (Arc<dyn Addr>); nil slices are empty vectors or Option; time.Time deadlines are rust_stdlib::time::Time (zero means none); nil-pointer receivers are not representable. The pure-Go resolver (Resolver{prefer_builtin: true, dial: ...}) is a Rust port that reads /etc/resolv.conf, /etc/hosts and /etc/nsswitch.conf and speaks DNS over UDP/TCP; without prefer_builtin, host and IP lookups use the system resolver through ToSocketAddrs. Randomised orders (MX ties, SRV weights) differ run to run as in Go. Operations that need system calls std lacks are implemented in rust_stdlib_sys::net (crates/sys, ADR 0004) and mapped there: Interfaces, InterfaceAddrs, InterfaceByName/Index and the Interface methods (getifaddrs), SetLinger/SetReadBuffer/SetWriteBuffer/SetKeepAlive*, SyscallConn, ReadMsg*/WriteMsg*, Dial/Listen and their Dialer/ListenConfig options (local address, Control, KeepAlive, MultipathTCP, ip:* and unixpacket networks), ListenMulticastUDP, File{Conn,Listener,PacketConn} and IPConn. The sys option functions take any AsRawFd socket. rust_stdlib_sys::net also provides Go-shaped TCPConn, UDPConn, UnixConn, TCPListener and UnixListener over a poll(2) descriptor with a wake-up pipe, which its Dial/Listen family and Accept return: SetDeadline, SetReadDeadline, SetWriteDeadline and Close from another thread wake a blocked call at once, as in Go (the Close and deadline symbols of those five types are mapped there; the root crate's std-based types remain for callers who do not need the sys crate and take effect within about 50 ms). Raw IP and unixpacket success paths need root and a kernel with AF_UNIX sequenced packets, and are differentially covered only through their error paths on hosts without them. LookupAddr, LookupCNAME and the Resolver methods are rust_stdlib_sys::net, the cgo-resolver path (getnameinfo, res_search), differentially tested against Go in tools/dns_check.py (lookup_probe); the root crate's own lookup_addr/lookup_cname remain the pure resolver.

net::http: Go's net/http over a synchronous, thread-per-connection server and a pooling Transport. Request, Response, Client, Server, Handler, ServeMux, Transport, Cookie and Header are the one implementation of each concept (also reachable from their modules: request, response, client, server, handler, servemux, transport, cookie, header). HTTP/1.1 and, through net::http::h2, HTTP/2. TLS comes from the rust-stdlib-tls backend through the TlsConfig hook. See docs/HTTP.md.

net::http::cgi: the host Handler (environment construction, header parsing, internal redirects, error responses) and the child-side Request, RequestFromMap and Serve, verified against Go with scripted CGI programs and environments

net::http::cookiejar: Go's RFC 6265 jar with Options and PublicSuffixList, Go's storage, matching, ordering and Punycode host rules, differential-checked by tools/cookiejar_check.py; cookies carry Go's Quoted flag, times have nanosecond resolution, and the golang.org/x/net/idna mapping tables beyond lower-casing are not ported

net::http::fcgi: the responder role over a Listener, byte-identical records (including Go's buffering of the response stream), GetValues, aborts and unknown record types, verified against Go with scripted record streams
net::http::httptest: the recorder implements http::ResponseWriter and the server wraps http::server::Server. Go's panics on misuse are errors. TLS servers come from rust_stdlib_tls::httptest.

net::http::httptrace: every hook, wired into the Go-shaped Transport (connection acquisition, idle pool, DNS and connect via the context's net trace, TLS handshakes, request writing, Expect: 100-continue, 1xx and first-byte reads); hook order verified against Go with scripted servers. HTTP/2 connections fire the hooks where Go's http2 transport does (WroteHeaderField per HPACK field, WroteHeaders, Wait100Continue, WroteRequest, GotFirstResponseByte, Got1xxResponse, Got100Continue), verified over cleartext HTTP/2 with prior knowledge against Go
net::http::httputil: dumps, the chunked codec, ClientConn, ServerConn, ProxyRequest and ReverseProxy over net::http::Request and Response. See docs/HTTP.md.

net::http::pprof: Cmdline and the Index page and the Symbol/Handler request handling are byte-identical to Go (verified with tools/pprof_check.py); Go's runtime profiles (goroutine, heap, allocs, block, mutex, threadcreate, goroutineleak, CPU, execution trace, program-counter symbols) are views of the Go runtime and do not exist for Rust programs, so those endpoints are the deviation go-runtime-profiles. register_profile adds custom profiles (runtime/pprof.NewProfile) and register_default_handlers mounts the five endpoints on the default mux as importing Go's package does

net::mail: Addresses/lists/groups, Go address formatting, RFC 2047 names with charset hook, lenient message headers and Go date layouts (dates are time::Time parsed with Go's layouts); text is UTF-8 only

Addr is std::net::IpAddr plus an optional zone and delegates zone-free predicates and accessors to std (is_loopback, is_multicast, is_unspecified, to_canonical for Unmap and the canonical forms, Ipv4Addr::is_link_local/is_private/is_broadcast, to_ipv4_mapped for Is4In6, octets, to_bits for Next/Prev); IPv6 link-local unicast, unique-local (private), interface/link-local multicast stay ours because std's versions are unstable, and the Go-only parts (zones, Prefix, text forms) are ours. net::netip is Go's netip: Addr/AddrPort/Prefix value types with Go's exact ParseAddr/ParsePrefix/ParseAddrPort grammar and error texts, zones, IPv4-mapped forms and text/binary codecs, convertible to and from std::net. The zero Addr is Addr::default(). Zones are Rust strings, so non-UTF-8 zone bytes in UnmarshalBinary become U+FFFD; Marshal*/Append* return Result like Go's (T, error); Prefix::bits returns isize (-1 when invalid); As4 panics like Go (and so does Result::unwrap, which MustParse* maps to).

net::rpc is Go's net/rpc over rust_stdlib::reflect: a service is a #[derive(Reflect)] type whose #[reflect_methods] block has methods shaped like Go's (`&mut T2` for the reply pointer, Result<(), String> for error, `&mut self` for a pointer receiver), and Register applies Go's suitableMethods rules and messages. The gob wire (Request and Response headers named net/rpc.Request and net/rpc.Response, one gob Encoder per connection, buffered writes flushed per response), the server loop (a thread per call, responses serialized, error responses with the invalid-request placeholder body, ill-formed/unknown service and method texts), the client (pending calls, Go with a Done channel, shutdown and EOF mapping), HTTP CONNECT (ServeHTTP, HandleHTTP, DialHTTP) and the /debug/rpc page are verified by tools/rpc_check.py against live Go peers in both directions. Rust-shaped differences: arguments and replies are reflect Values (the typed Client::call copies in and out); registered receivers live in the dynamic store, so calls of `&mut self` methods of one service run one at a time; errors are the cloneable rpc::Error enum; Done channels are std SyncSenders whose capacity cannot be checked.

net::rpc::jsonrpc is Go's JSON-RPC 1.0 codec pair: {"method","params":[P],"id"} requests and {"id","result","error"} responses, one JSON value per line, ids kept as raw JSON (null when absent), Go's request-body, response-header and invalid-error handling, and the argument and reply JSON written by a private reflect-to-JSON bridge that follows encoding/json (field tags, omitempty/omitzero/string, embedded structs, sorted map keys, base64 []byte, HTML escaping, UnmarshalTypeError texts with the v1-on-v2 field paths). Custom MarshalJSON, UnmarshalJSON, MarshalText and UnmarshalText methods are called as encoding/json calls them: method sets and addressability decide which methods apply, a JSON method wins over a text method, MarshalJSON output is compacted with HTML escaping, UnmarshalJSON receives the exact input text, text is written as a JSON string, UnmarshalText receives the unquoted string, map keys are written and read through MarshalText and UnmarshalText when their types have them, and an error from any of these methods is reported with Go's text, the first error kept, a map key whose pointer alone has MarshalText fails with jsontext's member-name error (offset and JSON pointer of the response or request document), map keys are read through UnmarshalText only and the ,string option does not apply to fields read through a method. tools/rpc_check.py sends 120 raw request lines to Go and Rust servers and compares the response bytes, and runs live clients against both.

net::smtp: Go's client commands, error texts and extension handling verified byte for byte against Go with scripted servers; TLS is the TlsConfig hook and CRAM-MD5 takes the HMAC-MD5 function as a parameter because the root crate has neither TLS nor cryptography

net::textproto: Lines, continued lines, response codes, dot reader/writer, MIME headers with Go validation and explicit budgets; Pipeline, Conn (full duplex over one stream), NewConn, Dial and Go's error texts; UTF-8 text only (byte variants exist for lines); tools/textproto_check.py compares framing, error text and loopback Cmd/ReadResponse transcripts with Go

net::url is Go's generic URI parser (Parse, ParseRequestURI, ResolveReference, JoinPath, escaping, Values, ParseQuery) with Go's error texts, urlstrictcolons default and 10000-parameter limit. Strings are Rust Strings: percent-decoded components that are not UTF-8 hold U+FFFD (raw_path, raw_fragment and raw_query keep the encoded bytes so String round-trips them, the host and userinfo also keep their raw bytes, so String prints a non-UTF-8 %XX there unchanged); EscapeError holds bytes. Error.Timeout/Temporary delegate to the wrapped error for this crate's error types and io::Error.

std::fs / std::env / std::process behind Go's API (Unix only). Errors are io::Error values carrying PathError, LinkError, SyscallError, the io/fs and os sentinels and Errno, printed with Go's messages; is_exist/is_not_exist/is_permission/is_timeout and Error::is(&err) classify them. Root (OpenRoot, OpenInRoot and every Root method), ProcAttr.Files and Process.WithHandle are rust_stdlib_sys::os, built on openat/unlinkat/... and fork/execve with Go's traversal rules; the root crate's own os::Root and os::start_process remain the std-only versions. Root results are differentially tested against Go in tools/os_check.py (root_probe) and the exec pieces in tools/exec_check.py. Getuid/Geteuid/Getgid/Getegid/Getppid/Getgroups/Hostname, Process.Pipe (a real pipe(2)/pipe2(O_CLOEXEC) pair of Files with deadlines), Signal, Chtimes, Link and the File deadline methods (pipes, terminals and sockets; ErrNoDeadline otherwise) are rust_stdlib_sys::os, the system-interface crate of ADR 0004, which calls the C library directly and is differentially tested against Go in tools/sys_check.py.

Cmd over std::process::Command (Unix only). StdinPipe, StdoutPipe and StderrPipe return a PipeEnd (a shared handle on the pipe's File) that Wait closes after the process exits, as in Go. Standard streams are Input/Output enums (a File is passed directly, a reader or writer goes through a pipe and a thread). LookPath uses Go's rules including ErrDot. Output/CombinedOutput return (data, result). Cmd.ExtraFiles and Cmd.Start are rust_stdlib_sys::os::exec::Cmd (fork/execve: ExtraFiles at descriptors 3 and up, "exec format error" for a file without a shebang, and a WaitDelay that closes the parent's pipe ends to interrupt copier threads, without CommandContext or Cancel), differentially tested against Go in tools/exec_check.py; the root crate's Cmd stays on std::process and still cannot honor ExtraFiles or SysProcAttr.

rust_stdlib_sys::os::signal over sigaction and a self-pipe read by one thread, as Go's runtime queues signals for its signal loop: per-channel masks, reference counts, non-blocking delivery that drops for full channels, Stop waiting for queued signals, Go's Ignore/Reset/Ignored state machine, and NotifyContext. Real-signal differential in tools/signal_check.py; SIGURG is relayed like any other signal, and SIGPROF is swallowed by the profiler handler as in Go (Notify keeps the process alive and delivers nothing)

Go's cgo build (the default on Linux and macOS): rust_stdlib_sys::os::user looks accounts up through the C library (getpwuid_r, getpwnam_r, getgrgid_r, getgrnam_r, getgrouplist), so NSS, LDAP and Open Directory users resolve, with Go's buffer-growth loop and error texts. Go's pure osusergo build (an /etc/passwd and /etc/group parser) is not provided. Differential in tools/os_user_check.py against Go's cgo build.
path: Slash-only clean/join/base/dir/ext/split and Unicode shell patterns; UTF-8 paths only

Unix rules (separator /, list separator :, no volumes); Windows volume and UNC rules are not implemented and the module is Unix only. UTF-8 &str paths. Clean, Split, Join, Base, Dir, Ext and IsAbs are shared with the path package; Match, Rel, IsLocal, Localize, EvalSymlinks, Glob and WalkDir (an iterator; Walk is WalkDir::list_first) are ports of Go's algorithms over os.

plugin: a permanent deviation (ADR 0004). Go plugins are shared objects built by the Go toolchain and loaded into a Go runtime that shares its type tables; Rust has neither. The surface exists and Open fails with "plugin: not implemented", as Go's stub does on platforms without plugin support

Rust has no run-time reflection, so reflect is opt-in: the Reflect trait (derived by rust-stdlib-derive, implemented here for the standard types) gives each Rust type a Go type descriptor and copies values in and out of a dynamic, aliasing store. Type is an interned handle (equal exactly when Go types are identical), with Go's type strings, struct tags, method sets, assignability, convertibility and amd64 layout. Value implements Go's addressability and CanSet rules, calls, Convert (Go's numeric wraparound and string rules), maps, slices, channels and select. Methods panic where Go's do (ValueError payloads). Values are copies: reflect::edit is the idiom for ValueOf(&x).Elem().Set(...). Option maps to a pointer; Box/Rc/Arc are transparent; tuples map to structs. Float to integer Convert is exact where Go defines it (in range); out-of-range and NaN results are implementation-defined in Go and follow Rust saturation here. Interop: fmt::Value and text/template::Value are built from reflect::Value (From impls); encoding/json keeps its typed Serialize path and has no conversion.

regexp: Go 1.27 semantics (leftmost-first; leftmost-longest for POSIX and Longest), linear time, on Go's three matchers chosen as Go's find does: one-pass, the bit-state backtracker, and the Pike VM. nil slices become Option or an empty Vec, unmatched groups are None (-1 in submatch index vectors), single matches are (start, end) tuples, readers take RuneReader/Utf8RuneReader over io::Read. patterns are &str, so invalid-UTF-8 patterns cannot be passed. Additions without a Go symbol: find_index_at and find_submatch_index_at expose the search from an offset that Go runs internally (FindAll), and find_anchored_index_at and find_anchored_submatch_index_at accept only a match beginning at the offset.

regexp/syntax: port of parse, simplify, compile and the prog dumps, checked against Go on thousands of patterns. Flags, Op, InstOp, EmptyOp and ErrorCode are newtypes with associated constants. Sub holds Arc<Regexp>; parse takes &str and parse_bytes takes bytes (the only way to reach ErrInvalidUTF8); Error.Expr is lossy UTF-8. Go's limits (maxHeight 1000, maxSize, maxRunes) are kept.

slices: std slice, Vec and Iterator methods. Go's BinarySearch is the leftmost position (partition_point), CompactFunc compares with the original predecessor (rust_stdlib::collections::compact_by), and float ordering and Min/Max follow Go's NaN rules through rust_stdlib::math::{compare, minimum, maximum}. SortFunc and SortedFunc are rust_stdlib::collections::sort_unstable_by, Go's own algorithm, so equal elements are ordered as in Go; the stable sorts are std's, whose order is unique; MaxFunc needs .rev() to return Go's first maximum and CompareFunc/EqualFunc are zip expressions (see each note).

sort: std slice methods. Go's unstable sort is pdqsort and its order of equal elements is deterministic; where equal elements are distinguishable (Sort, Slice, Float64s) the mapping is rust_stdlib::collections::sort_unstable_by[_less], a port that reproduces it (tests/collections_sort.rs); for integers and strings std's sort_unstable is exact. Go's NaN-first float order is rust_stdlib::math::compare; sort.Interface (Len/Less/Swap over any type) is a slice plus Ord, so the Interface-based entry points collapse into the slice methods.

strconv: Go's syntax and error rules over Rust std digit generation and parsing. Go's (value, error) returns map to Result; the NumError keeps the value Go returns with the error (int_value, uint_value, float_value, complex_value: Inf or max-magnitude on ErrRange). Itoa, FormatBool and the decimal cases of FormatInt/ParseFloat are to_string/str::parse in Rust; the Go-exact pieces (base prefixes and underscores, 'g'/'e' with precision -1, quoting) stay. Strings are bytes (AsRef<[u8]>); runes are i32/u32/char via the Rune trait; complex128 is strconv::Complex; an invalid FormatFloat/FormatInt base or bit size panics as in Go (a programming error, not input).

Go's strings are byte strings that may hold invalid UTF-8. For valid text the symbol is std (`str` methods, `String`, `slice::join`); `tools/strings_check.py` runs both std and `BytesExt` against Go on valid UTF-8 and checks they agree. Where std differs (empty separators, Go's simple case mapping, EqualFold, cutset-free predicates on invalid bytes) it is `rust_stdlib::text::BytesExt` on `&[u8]`, with Go's U+FFFD-of-width-1 rule. Reader and Replacer are `rust_stdlib::text`. Go index -1 is Option<usize>; runes are char.

sync: std::sync (Mutex, RwLock, Condvar, Once, OnceLock). Go's lock/unlock become holding and dropping a guard. sync.Map is Mutex<HashMap>, sync.Pool is Mutex<Vec> with a constructor, and only WaitGroup (a counter shared with detached threads) is first-party, in rust_stdlib::concurrent.

sync/atomic: std::sync::atomic. Go's Add returns the new value (fetch_add returns the old one, so add the delta back with wrapping_add); And and Or return the old value like fetch_and and fetch_or; CompareAndSwap is compare_exchange(..).is_ok(). Pointer[T] is AtomicPtr<T>; Value is an RwLock around the stored value; Rust types are static, so Go's inconsistent-type panic cannot happen in typed code (examples/stdsync_probe.rs simulates Go's dynamic slot only to match the oracle).

syscall: linux/amd64 constants, struct layouts and zsyscall wrappers generated by tools/gen_syscall.go from Go's own sources into rust_stdlib_sys::syscall; hand-written helpers port the rest. System calls run for real on linux/x86_64 (extern "C" syscall from the C library); other targets get the portable libc subset (read, write, close, dup, fsync, ftruncate, the id and process queries, umask, wait4, fork/exec) and ENOSYS for the rest. Errno and Signal use the Linux tables on every host. Names are snake_case functions and SCREAMING constants; Go struct names are kept (Stat_t, RawSockaddrInet4). Go's int is isize, uint and uintptr are usize, string is &str, []byte is &[u8] or &mut [u8], pointers are references (Option for nil-able ones). Wrappers return Result<T, Errno> and drop Go's raw result on failure.

Go's testing package: T, B, F, M, PB and the TB trait with Go's report format (--- FAIL lines, indented logs, === RUN/PAUSE/CONT/NAME/ATTR in verbose mode, benchmark result lines), usable from Rust #[test] functions through testing::run_test and the test_fn! macro or as a whole test binary through main_start/M::run. Fatal, FailNow, Skip and SkipNow unwind with the Goexit payload (testing::is_goexit). Log/Error/Fatal/Skip take a slice of Display operands (fmt.Sprintln) and the *f forms take format_args!. Subtests: T::run runs inline (may borrow), T::run_static on a thread (parallel). Cleanup closures are 'static. Differences are recorded as deviations; allocation statistics need an allocator calling testing::record_alloc.

Lives in rust-stdlib-crypto because it replaces the generator of crypto/rand (rust_stdlib cannot depend on the crypto crate). The stream is SHA-256 in counter mode over the seed, not ChaCha8, so bytes differ from Go's for a given seed (the way algorithms consume randomness is unspecified in Go as well).

MapFS and MapFile are the in-memory file system of rust_stdlib::io::fs (re-exported here), including Go's symlink resolution in Open, Lstat and ReadLink and MapFile.Sys. TestFS is a port of testfs.go: the same checks and error texts (verified against Go on generated and corrupted trees by tools/testing_check.py); the error is an io::Error wrapping a TestFSError that lists the problems. Files expose Seek and ReaderAt through File::as_seek/as_reader_at, the counterparts of Go's type assertions.

Readers and writers as std::io wrappers; ErrTimeout is the unit type ErrTimeout (ERR_TIMEOUT, is_err_timeout) converting to an io::Error of kind TimedOut. The loggers write through rust_stdlib::log::printf. Behaviour is compared with Go by tools/testing_check.py (wrapper scripts and TestReader verdicts over deliberately broken readers).

Generator is a static trait (Rust has no zero value to call a method on); built-in impls follow quick.go's sizedValue draw for draw over math/rand (v1), so a seed gives Go's values (checked by tools/testing_check.py). The default count honours -quickchecks; Config.Rand is consumed by a check and restored afterwards.

The same 17 cases and checks as Go. Results are json::Value objects (Go's map[string]any); parse the handler's JSON with rust_stdlib::encoding::json. The explanations carry the Rust source position of the case. Verdicts for a JSON handler broken by ReplaceAttr transforms are compared with Go by tools/testing_check.py.
Fake-clock bubble over threads (see the fake-runtime deviation). Traces of sleeps, waits, goroutines and channels are compared with Go's synctest by tools/testing_check.py.

rust_stdlib::text::scanner: Go's tokenizer ported literally (same buffers, read sizes, error texts and positions), over std::io::Read. Token text is returned as bytes because Go strings may hold invalid UTF-8. tests/text_scanner.rs ports scanner_test.go (tables generated from the Go source); tools/text_scanner_check.py compares tokens, positions, error callbacks, Peek/Next and Read-call counts with Go over 6000 vectors. Error messages written to standard error without a callback are not compared.
tabwriter: Incremental elastic tab stops and Go flags; explicit section/cell/column/output budgets; Writer<W> is statically typed, so Init takes the same writer type

text/template: Template is a handle (clone = copy of Go's *Template; Clone is clone_template, New is associated). Execution runs over the typed Value model in text::template::value instead of reflect; data comes from the ToValue trait and functions from Value::func_of or the func0..func4/variadic builders. Funcs and Option panic on bad input like Go; strings are UTF-8; variadic arguments reach callables flattened; ParseFS takes any io::fs::FS (DirFS, MapFS, embed::FS) with fs.Glob semantics.

text/template/parse: lexer, parser and AST are a port of Go's. Nodes own their children, so Copy is Clone and Tree.Parse fills in the receiver instead of returning it; nodes record their tree for delimiters and error context in a shared TreeInfo. String methods are the Display impls.
time: Go Time/Duration/Location with TZif zones (system, ZONEINFO, embedded tzdata feature), Format/Parse, timers and tickers on std threads; TZif versions 1 to 3 as Go 1.27 (version 4 is malformed)

unicode: range tables generated from Go's unicode package by tools/unicode_gen.go (Unicode 17.0.0); runes are i32; Go maps are sorted slices of pairs; In takes a slice (in_); IsControl is std char::is_control (compared against Go by tools/unicode_check.py); IsSpace is std char::is_whitespace

std covers UTF-16: `char::encode_utf16`, `char::decode_utf16` (unpaired surrogates become U+FFFD) and `char::len_utf16`; tools/unicode_check.py compares them against Go. Only the surrogate-pair helpers on i32 runes are in `rust_stdlib::unicode::rune`.

Go's lossy decoding (every ill-formed byte is a width-1 U+FFFD) lives in `rust_stdlib::unicode::rune`, on i32 runes so invalid values can be passed; validity is `std::str::from_utf8`. The `*InString` forms are the same functions: a Go string is `&[u8]`.
unique: Arc-based interning table keyed by TypeId; entries are swept as the table grows (Go uses the GC).

rust_stdlib::uuid: RFC 9562 UUIDs as a [u8; 16] newtype with Go's parsing rules (the four accepted forms, error text 'invalid uuid'), lowercase formatting, Compare and the NewV7 monotonic clock state (a process-wide mutex, as Go). Random bits come from /dev/urandom on Unix, the operating-system source that rust_stdlib::math::rand's seeding reads; the root crate has no dependencies, so platforms other than Unix have no std-only source and New, NewV4 and NewV7 panic there with Go's crypto/rand failure text (never a weaker source). tests/uuid.rs ports uuid_test.go (the synctest clock checks use the wall clock with a one-millisecond tolerance); tools/uuid_check.py compares 10,640 parse, format, compare and MustParse vectors with Go and checks 6,000 NewV4/NewV7 values by property on both sides.
weak: std::sync::Weak; Make is Arc::downgrade, Value is Weak::upgrade, equality is Weak::ptr_eq
